subject: MAGA's end-around the Constitution
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Integrity First Voter Action Project, www
body:
This is what it comes down to: The sitting President of the United States is trying to exert direct control over the U.S. Postal Service to get around the Constitution, which says that states have control of elections. Courts are stopping him from directly suppressing mail-in ballots, so he's trying an end run around them using USPS.
Trump and the MAGA movement want to pick and choose whose vote counts. RUSH $35 or whatever you can right now to fight back against this abuse of the USPS and our fundamental right to vote >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=061026_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
NYT: Trump Signs Order Seeking Federal Control of Mail Voting as He Promotes False Claims [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=061026_3&amount=25]
Straight from the New York Times , Team:
" President Trump on [March 31] stepped up efforts to promote his false claims of widespread voting fraud, signing an executive order of questionable constitutionality seeking to create a national list of citizens that would determine voting eligibility and restrict mail ballots. "
Let's be clear: The president has no explicit Constitutional authority over elections, and much of this latest attack on our fundamental right to vote appears difficult to enforce and legally dubious.
This order directs the Department of Homeland Security to create a “ state citizenship list ” based on data from various federal databases. It also directs federal officials to send that made-up list to state election officials, and orders the attorney general to prioritize prosecution of election officials who provide ballots to voters not on the made-up list. It also directs the U.S. Postal Service not to transmit mail-in ballots from any individual not included on Trump's “ state citizenship list ," even though elections are mandated by the constitutional the be run by the states.
This order is yet another sign that the MAGA crew will do anything they can to codify their power permanently and silence the will of the people by suppressing and eliminating the votes we cast.
Our elections are sound and mail-in voting is secure, no matter what Trump says. Step up to defend our fundamental right to vote and the use of mail-in ballots with $35 or whatever you can today >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=061026_3&amount=35]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?express_lane=true&refcode=061026_3&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?express_lane=true&refcode=061026_3&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?express_lane=true&refcode=061026_3&amount=50]

We all know that mail-in voting laws are about ballot accessibility, making it easier for voters to participate in our elections . States have spent millions of taxpayer dollars investigating voter fraud since 2020's "big lie" and found virtually nothing. It's been used widely in some states for decades and in most of the country since the pandemic.
But that doesn't stop Trump because he's absolutely terrified of what might happen in the next election.
Arizona’s Secretary of State (the official who runs elections), Adrian Fontes, reacted like this: “ The Constitution doesn’t allow the executive to take over elections administration, that’s a job for the state legislatures or Congress, and so I don’t think this is going to pass any sort of judicial muster. So this is a big, giant waste of time, and it’s an attention grab from the Trump administration. ”
He added: “ The greatest threat to American elections is Donald Trump lying about them. ” That''s because Donald Trump’s continued claims about large-scale “cheating” in elections are outright lies.
Protecting vote-by-mail for the upcoming midterms is crucial to make every voice heard in our elections. Will you chip in $35 or whatever you can to fight lies about mail-in voting and help make every vote count? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=061026_3&amount=35]

name: Newt Gingrich
subject: Somebody has to say what nobody wants to hear
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the NRSC
body:
|
Peter, it's Newt Gingrich.

I am going to be straight with you, because that is the only way I know how to operate.

Trump Signs $70B ICE Bill

President Trump signed the [Secure America Act](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0LuOhSAYBOCngU7zw-GAFhTb2J1ttzTc1D_hFsH19Te-wjaTKSZfMT-f9WMwYt6_TQoaW1t98WtzJnsTazT7FXyNpudw3pjbyoHLAeTAYK1naTW4vnLq9ZuzaZto0ExNjL3kDBM9tLRezZILIWE2EKw3ahIABrYwT8wKivoBQTIGwN6gRgZvKfwGYlMva2dLBFzVmx5GzA19aK6UWkvEjq6N5dxp1EfvtZHXF-EL4ct936PL1o2uJMKXxyd8gScYEL7080p1QBcGBYPFGLHkAVPC_TT96duVPeZ9PHqK9NS-3s-oSUUE7MlgfGTa_33Wr-Z_AQAA__8rxnpx) on Wednesday, delivering $70 billion in funding for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) through the end of his term. The bill passed the House on Tuesday along strict party lines after four months of Republican infighting. Democrats demanded agency reforms and accountability measures; Republicans refused, and the bill cleared without a [single Democratic vote](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D1yhSAUQOHVQKfD5QloQZHG7qVN6fDruzMIjGDcfsYtpDvVV5yf9_Y2mDDv3-YIGlvbfPFbcyZ7k2oy-xV8TabncN6Y28YZlwOTA7CtnqXV4PrGqdeCwxxnGjSoGeAlFzbTjxY2AnhlwKiFWSG9gIVP0Qg3KzGJSFE_IJMAjIFgagQm5OQjm6J6WbtYMrGretPDiLmhD82VUmtJ2NG1sZw7TfrTe23k9UX4Svh63_fobMvhbqMrB-Hrk4Sv_byOOuBx4H6ajiUP8coe8z5YTGlAFwhf6al9vTElbFKRie2HwfQ4tP_7zq_mfwEAAP__msd3qA). ICE gets $46 billion, CBP gets $24 billion—funding both agencies through January 2029. The signing closes the spring's defining domestic policy fight and hands Trump a clean win on his top legislative priority before the midterm cycle shifts into [high gear](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0E0OnSAUQOHV4AwDF0UdMOjE2eu0Q8OfehMEwsW-7TftErqBc5Lv1-f4WEyYr5_2iQaJjlDCQd7mYFNN9npjqMn2HNsXMx0gQHOhuRRHbYVq9P2AIZgZ5HquQzRyWaVUehPrcJtNrRAdTF6oSW3a6Q2CXrRy4bTbos8Bzd-g0FIKIWexjFLMegqnmM5FObc5Nom3BtvjiJkwRPKl1FoSdvQ0lnYNydy9V2LqB4Odwd7veGNKoy8Pg_0uT8zxSwx2Gx7MSL3ZjiUz2OdNrgqA9_Y-lRNembjDlPj55oD54ugj99XxfrfyXjen6EsOvMf2DM2E-sWUkPTCJnE9Fv89h_7fir8N_AkAAP__DnuFtg). ★★★
US Strikes Iran Again Today

President Trump announced Wednesday that U.S. forces would strike Iran ["hard again today,"](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0DvOnDAQAODTmM5obN6FizR0mzYlGj9gRzFgecz6-tEqN_gv8BXfn9f2Qop0Hb_xDIaYN3_7jR1eHmOKeDzBp4jlCrnSxZsGPUoYpYIt5ZtTcGXTjTeDVvM-N8GoaVaqGxeYm7cB37lhH3CZnJ0d9nuHi907UJO1c_DQkPmCMCoFoAaYWgXD2Psd-n3qrF2s6OFJHkto6WLygd19p3RHKuS4vfPRRPMuJbHofgm9Cr3WWltn-QqVW3efQq-RPkH-V1jolTJesmKWJT9nkg9LLpn-BpaY0L2D0GuTjU-VYiQeJ9HDcSLFr9aUHx99jP4XAAD__1G0erU) hours after Tehran launched retaliatory missile attacks on U.S. allies Bahrain and Kuwait. The escalation comes as Trump simultaneously claims a peace deal is "days away"—a posture that has defined the conflict since U.S. and Israeli forces launched joint strikes on Iran in February. Trump says maximum pressure is the strategy; [critics say he is negotiating and bombing at the same time](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0DGOhSAYBODTQKf5QQQsKLaxe9tuaVDQ9ycIBPCZvf3GK2wz1eSbZH5ey8tiwHh829MbrHVxyS11s9HZkIM9Lu9ysC36cmOsCwcuO5AdgyWXVLPf2sKpMyNnetfUG6Y0Y4OcQNO3mZgcdy3UCoP3wMU48smrXYBlu56UpmgeECRjAGwE1TMYpXA7iF0N6zqtRMCVnW2-x1jR-bqllHMK2HCrfSoHDebdWq5k-CJ8Jny-77uPvw1PX_stnYTPAT-e8PlZInyGJxg8zVSCI3zGYmN329K1cp25uyotxuUbQ8AqFRFwnBbDg9H274s-hv8FAAD__waadhA). The U.S. also confirmed it disabled an Iranian tanker in the Gulf of Oman on Wednesday, with three crewmembers reported missing. Trump declared the U.S. ["controls the Strait of Hormuz, not Iran."](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0L2ynDAMhuGrMZ0Z28vyU1CkoTtpUzLC0rJKjO2xzHL7GZI7OK2K99F8v77WL-DAcf8JB80ssmLCVTxEhJAD7CdhDlAjlYujrM64XpteW7PmkiSTr6trcH46O77GhmY7jNY--smMzXumoUOYhqkbup7ME8yIjiYi_8DRb5treL6DprfWGPs0Q2vNs-_wZbrX8Ni2aVOdOTNCpZajMJL4lHJOgSt7aVPZmzC_a82iHj-UW5Rbrutq65v2EwoyxNan476mElC5JfCHlFtuVbnl9xmVW6xRbuECUV9Q9H9O9MEiHEhLLfyHRNdyHlmfogtVCAyVU9QHIwbSBFK1Lyws_xq30pQZ88UhsPSD6sx-AIf7m6Z-e-fP7P4GAAD__x7Xklg) ★★★
SCOTUS Mail-In Ballot Ruling Due

The Supreme Court is in the final stretch of its term with a consequential ruling pending on whether states can count [mail-in ballots that arrive after Election Day](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0LHupiAQBPCnwU6zoIIWFNfYfddeaRBW3WQVAnjf61_MvcG_nl9mkvnzWT-OmO7jt7vQUilriGEt3t3BcWJ3PBgSu3pj_tJdVgVKt6BbCWvKsST0dVVNsKOS0z41aKWZpOz1DFNz2nnGfRynqUcjdzDGea-V7ncT_DgM_dSQfQtBSwkgRzCdhFEPYYdhN_22zZsY4EnBVezoLhSw-BhTikyVfOliPhq2Z62piP6XUItQSz3xJObOx0uoJePxsKsUb6EWH59c283VyliEWsZZGtC6LU_KeGH7P78ccUt3uznmWF_XZBvSl5ipaCMGOF7yDjT1x5f9tepfAAAA__8YMH34). The case centers on a Mississippi law allowing late-arriving ballots. If the conservative majority strikes it down, grace periods in California and several other states would be invalidated—directly reshaping how [November's midterms are counted](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0L3SpCAQheGrwUyraX8nINjEbDbd0EJona4CoWjc2cvf8ha-5AQneIL3z3t7Ww58nb9tJMMim09-E2cvb0MO9rzJ52DrReXLl2wIOLUwtRq2XJJkcnXDxpsR9XIsDRk9L1r30wuW5mP6Gfpln3ZH-zHS8ELCBWke92G2dCzYsHlAmLQG0CPMnYZxGvwBwzH3-_7a1QB39rZSx5ewJ3Ep5ZwCV3bSpXI2wXxqzaL6XwpXhav9x0k6l6LC9cEVrvCMBoWr3LlQpNalu9S2ljvmlgK5yumSNrKvVKK0HCOfxT5vU4zPXw6BZZrVAGe0HB6-qT_O9dfg_wAAAP__J1585A) in states where late mail is common. NPR reports the ruling could also affect Alaska, where extreme weather routinely delays ballot delivery. A decision is expected within weeks, before state election officials begin [finalizing midterm procedures](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0DEO3CAQheHT4G4swAa8BUUad5s2pTUL410kFpAHx8ntI18hzWue9BX_r-f2xJRTef_EL_nEvMUaNw5YIuaW8X1SbBl7oeNKhTcttQVpQcmtHZUbhb7pIXqj1bIvA3nlFqUm-5DL8PHGTg-ng1Oo3WRsjFa56MKitJmdcWFI_galVUpKZaQblTR2jrucdze9Xo-XmOXZInYaU-EUiUOtrdWcego81uM9ZP_pvbGYfgi9Cr1e1zWWdtyf0OvNC73Ke5QUei1_gBWYRVq9GKFXDrWfDJFC4lQL1AJfTBlSgRfmXDtDqGeOgPtOoQN37MRwfegguAj7hw4IWCDgyQSRMv7l4fCxXSnnxNaJWb5vcgz1O_T_bvzb638BAAD__yFQjNU).

name: Mike Rogers
subject: I saw Osama bin Laden's cold, dead body.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Rogers for Senate
body:
Here’s what the moment meant then, and what it means now.

| |
---

---
Friend, I've worn many hats in my life. I'm a proud husband and a father. I was the third of four generations in my family to serve in the United States military. I was an FBI agent in the early 90s -- back when we locked up bad guys like human traffickers and drug dealers. And in Congress, I served as the **Chairman of The House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.**
---
[ | It was in this capacity that I experienced one of the biggest defining moments of my life. On May 2, 2011 Osama bin Laden — the worst enemy America has ever known — was killed dead in his home by some of America's bravest heroes. Seeing the photo of Osama bin Laden's cold, dead body riddled with bullets was one of the most surreal moments I've ever experienced. In a weird way, it sent both a chill up my spine, while also bringing an indescribable level of calmness.
--- ](https://links.rogersforsenate.com/u/click?_t=293de5a6223e4436ab53fb8020578890&_m=3654996666254668874da3398badc7f0&_e=Y6tGrzJwFIvFzFhNbW9XqahpL8SU4LiX5l5KQMUtAbY-cIeUXemRis2ayHTe2mV2BV6zE9dNlIqxqNJLPe-YsOVdCrqT-4jY1u7UODfv9Ic8Meo6fNALgnwwvHJdQEm302d4JNFz6n3pDyGbZHZaCDqt9w9C-LjuhUl1p0kk0Qcgo7RKc6TnHluUEl4F9sEp0e-7QLyERXJVBUqaNTdp6C6vICugIFGnniMZAS2_3Cd_L0nAuDElCaHby_wzekOOAZtXG3-jScX7VFLh-frHNB9imiLmNQg-svVvcYIgRPkFMWaiNM58icyYiSbOGWmwJOE6YKJWMEvEYjOjiTdolnKRdJZi7fyiSQjn746qg-rc3NkriY0uKw0SDp6THnun6HfqGdFuvixIhZuD67gDrLwZsftKpsgME6NygG5V35U5G3buA-ygnccGHOU04Pl5XxRN8mUMW80z0pN4FAOdJmH-SdUkbe4N0gbswIJIWErYrC0bmbI9b2q-IMAoHVd7T_JQHdsS7U0U5k5z8Ud5ZXIO-dwTFrjWBg5q6VwJEOt2-HUD9eTIxLEpygXm2z0oeap8Miht8ujyZCZUB0hkEuhcBxbAewfN1zDhFOl9f94UWPUAnlMYM5Zxz_4UeiHvsArejepanCRslfRHZw_YRsHgIYpOL-zBffRdi6WcQvq3sgxHjWIP8edoJCrUVyb9eG3mfyH2D9zwaVd8rUm9H5S2I-HoguGartrzX6jfsio%3D)
10 years after the attacks on September 11th, and finally, we captured and killed the man responsible for shaking our nation to its core. But that calm feeling didn't last for long.
---
[ | You see, right now America is at a crossroads. We have foreign enemies trying to see to our downfall while radical, brainwashed sympathizers right here at home cheer it on.
--- ](https://links.rogersforsenate.com/u/click?_t=293de5a6223e4436ab53fb8020578890&_m=3654996666254668874da3398badc7f0&_e=Y6tGrzJwFIvFzFhNbW9XqahpL8SU4LiX5l5KQMUtAbY-cIeUXemRis2ayHTe2mV2BV6zE9dNlIqxqNJLPe-YsOVdCrqT-4jY1u7UODfv9Ic8Meo6fNALgnwwvHJdQEm302d4JNFz6n3pDyGbZHZaCDqt9w9C-LjuhUl1p0kk0Qcgo7RKc6TnHluUEl4F9sEp0e-7QLyERXJVBUqaNTdp6C6vICugIFGnniMZAS2_3Cd_L0nAuDElCaHby_wzekOOAZtXG3-jScX7VFLh-frHNL9-3Z65VRcqx_BxBGt5Fu_rKkrYK2o6VfBpbcgxmKRDPGut2T7HTrf6bRmxS2q71m0EQMjJ5TZsMxPaPsrUls5IzaAuIKKLK012emAzOom4YvalS8GSguauEUPOZiHTHIlNd24oJoEQj_k-LFU5pwETAc5fwchfqouH2Z-m91reGw7MThJK_LK4isZCHeh_4UucalsVhJkBRKcSTpO0gZD9yH5RowSR_HWOrGrEI6TODEIHFILNV9waiOVl4WCvUErVnMGxLGf-vHt2brAKyjcfauKowExRs8CFU9sUJv8aBVP60uz4T3iuCIpnk7-j5GyaPpUioG6ZmbezPeqOiiiIIsFUPoUg7KPo8j8yzJN-vmIa0uYayGr4VTT0eyICI6RqduxfEoq3mBWMVxUAQLnnZhHcKmWNp5DREZXyxWq6hv8wXsakI6FDtiTNjqSGyrPyUFG3nxlT7sD58iYxcoc%3D)
I say enough is enough.
---
[ | I've worn this nation's uniform as an officer in the United States Army. My father served in the Air Force. My brother served in the Army and fought in Iraq. My wife deployed to Iraq while working for the Department of Defense and **survived an IED explosion.** And most recently, our son served in the Navy. My family has given our blood, sweat, and tears to this country. And I'm damn proud that we did.
--- ](https://links.rogersforsenate.com/u/click?_t=293de5a6223e4436ab53fb8020578890&_m=3654996666254668874da3398badc7f0&_e=Y6tGrzJwFIvFzFhNbW9XqahpL8SU4LiX5l5KQMUtAbY-cIeUXemRis2ayHTe2mV2BV6zE9dNlIqxqNJLPe-YsOVdCrqT-4jY1u7UODfv9Ic8Meo6fNALgnwwvHJdQEm302d4JNFz6n3pDyGbZHZaCDqt9w9C-LjuhUl1p0kk0Qcgo7RKc6TnHluUEl4F9sEp0e-7QLyERXJVBUqaNTdp6C6vICugIFGnniMZAS2_3Cd_L0nAuDElCaHby_wzekOOAZtXG3-jScX7VFLh-frHNPVQTKZWEFx9WuCinHtuR2NMyW9KZqW1l-kLkz1D0bKb0MkMpfB_Lz3eVQ4askOTlaTqXjI_5NFqO2CC1VwkYVlfhkEYqEupElz3mkkM_h1yBtwR3quiyB4Ge9r7x3Ij7hCu-KxsPCSOA5lR0-mwtYTnj4MZbN7-kwZh2uUmDG_YRVDoBoLuOIp7YheNaVZf4R8Zgdr6U9QAUc8jgB-u1JuyZHm33MUic9LOOu9IadmJWjCu59obh_kiPoxrgPCUFAnl_eWpdYr1mSx5OqAmnNzQhnQZXxxKlmskYLIz35FTyIxWrU07Z2RwApiad14oakHyGXzj_GbzPw7edHRINZc5u-dRJEuAg8Dde0GgV72wMRareKCrw9nDSMQZePk1tOZtnNFxyTG0RmiBBs3JIAaJbfrYn3tbEbYTaRK_7M1871z0TRoqfZv_h7_ZhS9lkNw2JulBygrWsXvE7dGr10Q%3D)
But our fight is not over yet. President Trump has set out on a mission to undo all of the disasters of the last four years -- but not even he can do that alone. I'm running for the United States Senate to add one more hat to my shelf. This time, it's bright red and has four words written across the front:

clean_body: Here’s what the moment meant then, and what it means now. | | Friend, I've worn many hats in my life. I'm a proud husband and a father. I was the third of four generations in my family to serve in the United States military. I was an FBI agent in the early 90s -- back when we locked up bad guys like human traffickers and drug dealers. And in Congress, I served as the Chairman of The House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence. 10 years after the attacks on September 11th, and finally, we captured and killed the man responsible for shaking our nation to its core. But that calm feeling didn't last for long. I say enough is enough. But our fight is not over yet. President Trump has set out on a mission to undo all of the disasters of the last four years -- but not even he can do that alone. I'm running for the United States Senate to add one more hat to my shelf. name: Sherrod Brown
subject: NEW POLLING IN OHIO: 53-45
disclaimer_text: Paid for by State Democrats Committee (StateDemocrats
body:
A Fox News poll shows me ahead in Ohio’s Senate race.
#
Peter –
The first public poll of the general election in Ohio was just released, and you need to take a look:
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/105168?refcode=em20260610-10553&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=10553%2E614464%2Eu8iw3S)
This is a big deal. It’s the first public poll of the general election – and the data proves Ohio is ready to unseat my opponent, Jon Husted, and pave a path for us to flip the Senate in November.
**The momentum behind our campaign is growing, but so is the target on our backs. Republicans can see we’re putting up a fight, and they’re going to do whatever it takes to stop us in our tracks.[Before I say more, can you split any amount between my campaign and State Democrats Committee so we can hit our $100K rapid response goal and take on whatever’s next?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/105168?refcode=em20260610-10553&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=10553%2E614464%2Eu8iw3S)**
**[DONATE](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/105168?refcode=em20260610-10553&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=10553%2E614464%2Eu8iw3S)**
What we’re building together is truly remarkable, and I see it at every stop I make across the state. Folks are fed up with rising costs, rampant corruption, and a rigged system that makes it impossible to get ahead no matter how hard you work. So they’re showing up to make a change and proving that we have the support to flip this seat, even in a state Trump won by 11 points last time.
Seriously, we’re 8 points ahead of our opponent in this latest poll. _That’s the good news._
Here’s the tough part: Outside Republican groups and corporations see these polls, too. **They’ve already publicly announced I’m one of their top targets and are spending $83 million against me, so another poll like this will give them all the more reason to dump a fortune into Ohio to take me down.**
I don’t know what’s coming next, but I know the _only_ way we can keep this going in our favor is by fighting hard each and every day until the election. Ohio broke the record for the most expensive Senate race in history last time, so we need a lot of support if we’re going to pull this off.
**Your $5 might not seem like a lot on its own, but it all adds up when thousands of folks chip in whatever they can, whenever they can – even if it’s just $5 at a time.[If you’re with me, I’m earnestly asking if you can split a donation between my campaign and State Democrats Committee before midnight. Everything counts and means a ton to me personally.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/105168?refcode=em20260610-10553&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=10553%2E614464%2Eu8iw3S)**

[Contribute $5](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/105169?refcode=em20260610-10553&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=5&t=5&akid=10553%2E614464%2Eu8iw3S) [Contribute $15](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/105169?refcode=em20260610-10553&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=15&t=6&akid=10553%2E614464%2Eu8iw3S) [Contribute $30](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/105169?refcode=em20260610-10553&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=30&t=7&akid=10553%2E614464%2Eu8iw3S) [Contribute $50](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/105169?refcode=em20260610-10553&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=50&t=8&akid=10553%2E614464%2Eu8iw3S) [Contribute $100](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/105169?refcode=em20260610-10553&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=100&t=9&akid=10553%2E614464%2Eu8iw3S) [Contribute $250](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/105169?refcode=em20260610-10553&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=250&t=10&akid=10553%2E614464%2Eu8iw3S) [Give another amount](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/105168?refcode=em20260610-10553&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=11&akid=10553%2E614464%2Eu8iw3S)

My name is Tom Cotton. I grew up on my family's cattle farm in Dardanelle, Arkansas. My folks have farmed this land for seven generations. My dad worked for the state. My mom was a school teacher and later a principal.
[](https://links.trueamericanconservatives.com/s/c/rSEX_M6XjCTB29MbQdMWRtQ4AFGVdfCwvadDS80-GpRw3KxgZq3MeOAh61DWkx6UlCbjTgB_iqUTTLwZGpx-HpZHTDiNX4WoUQFdf41ZgiQxjiq1jTwJq7iLkQcnz_mK1UVp2tUvUEqx-2SwTnMYDCo4auHfUM3aPsdJi6cCLig9lglS06uJFYFMX62yfqNlPLgcAKTokmg30kFqh8gWZgnRMufmlQMB_SHB2VTZiHH6jcgms0DOyz2t0nFjxxlGEL4J5E9j9f5ZHJC5WSOlh4t50LDuK31ZzG7VXop1STD7YjA_ePRXvXmgFBAcF9X2LsPg6CQuCFIuj__0B68WK6dF05UNzahFizJm8v4fpA1FIdCZLfRxnUPQy3m-4vdE0IpzwD-9Pat1FVZjh29xFs8MDGr5-FGblh5nx_I-0cnlcM2ojArYRkZtYfK1yYXw8wxWDoF8u_swhDREUa7-4n9XmtVNP4YLtPcOZHTDiy6wwkNg8n90pgR7Zl5ypjqHb-lS-A8Qss14FIb4zHh7M0rm3mHMPMO75LIsR7NMt4hPJnnPTWk-4TE5RT7dp0HiipR42IEqtUrqYWo1uNWxeqWAeB9mS63PRSJmhDpAw5cAMZUx_dNig-xH_58WUqFcg-Maly7mjxvZBteHIS3uUyERStU66igTF4nVVTTnovoo_yS7W1PXB7zJ1s6ecMrbyhvX1vXx1jP5jb_12ggwqs_qzHLJ8QA-A00ZLcsiPtKTii--3CNUyNyVi36Z4g3Z8BuE71pt7jTtllbkNMtf3wAurIP8Xlb8Rw-ZNCcHfLelEHVW6J-uKNxSrhMo1jovoJNm7Z6T4zDl_ahf4fHlTJGRRrdS2BC9E9siVxWWeriL_9dfzBwm6tZ2vVJIoBjjk6Yw9EjRQEKBt7p-gLcuse5-1kdbRyMpCa49O_-QVuFJrvdpqSBNxk4/1cUYCxzocdLYSjbADPFC-cM-uSFocmsI/21)

_Then came September 11._

name: NHGOP Headquarters
subject: New Hampshire Republican Party Hires New Communications Director
body:
New Hampshire Republican Party Hires New Communications Director

| | | | | | |

---
| |

| | | | | | | **New Hampshire Republican State Committee Hires Karina Nicholas as Communications Director**
A few weeks ago, I announced that I was looking for funding to hire a Communications Director. Thanks in part to your donations, below is the press release announcing Karina’s hiring. She is going to be fabulous, and you will see a lot more messaging coming from the state party soon.

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE June 9th, 2026****CONTACT karina@nhrsc.com**
CONCORD, N.H. — The New Hampshire Republican State Committee (NHRSC) announced the hiring of Karina Nicholas as its new Communications Director.
A native of Stratham, Nicholas recently graduated from Hope College with a Bachelor of Arts in English. She joins the NHRSC after serving as an intern in Governor Chris Sununu's office in 2024 and as an assistant in the New Hampshire Senate Clerk's Office in 2025. Nicholas also serves as Communications Director for the New Hampshire Federation of Republican Women.
"We are excited to welcome Karina to the team," said Scott Maltzie, Chairman of the New Hampshire Republican State Committee. "Her passion for Republican principles, strong communications skills, and commitment to advancing our message make her a tremendous asset as we prepare for the upcoming election cycle."

Unfortunately, Rogers is firmly in the "I don't care about Americans' personal hardship" camp.
We deserve better.

# One Last Thought Until Next Week
---
| | |
---

When we started all of this, we came up with a four-phase plan:
Phase 1: Gather information on the district. This involved not only analytical research into the district but also visiting all 11 counties and talking to people about what they needed.

Phase 2: Meeting with democratic organizations in the district. This involved assessing the capacity of the existing party infrastructure to support a campaign.

Phase 3: Engage those party organizations to build a campaign network. This would include hiring essential professional staff.

Phase 4: Move outside the democratic organizations. Engaging independents and swayable Republicans in the run-up to the general election.
We are currently transitioning from Phase 3 to Phase 4 and working across all 11 counties. We have many great volunteers and hired professional staff with plans to bring on a few more essential staff members soon. We are beginning to place social media ad buys and stepping up our fundraising efforts to support this work. We are also in the final stages of planning town hall meetings and will make some announcements about them soon.
This week, I will send an email outlining specific ways you can support the campaign. Keep an eye out for that email, give it a read, and if you can help with any of the areas listed, we would really appreciate it.
We are gaining momentum across the district as we move ahead. We're making plans for the final run to the finish line in November. Your support has been great, and we're really looking forward to the next five months.
We are 147 days away from the general election.

We'll talk soon,

Lee

## Report: El Paso Detention Facility Wasted Millions
The rushed opening of Camp East Montana, the nation's largest immigration detention facility, led to up to [$11.5 million in wasted taxpayer money](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykUD2TpCAQ_TWYMdUwKBoQXEK2l15o9UC7UotiQe86_vsr7y9c8l7y6n39-Zg_MOW0f_7GjRy_lzLvdLZMzFTns9Qcw_fxlcJXK8vCK7WANdGsQQ8SBqnUHDHlazZddC-Ik-rIKTsqZXs7qW51xsA0GLtY9eqfL0VEPQEoE2KwMIxTl9xtBoNSSsETpkcPOoIhO0YkO40oDFBMXOqDV2J6Y1vyVX6oPkLZuuxW5qOJ5y-hvdD-PM_Hd0MuEa9bILRvXOoltL-X3YScyi60v3OF9nCDAqE9ZXlgKzLgdkjCxnIrO-OOMgWSC4aUE1-y0lEqyyXtsclIyGuTJzYmof0EZhz1aACs0L6rLh5nyjm1wQoDnxum_K82_9_ZP07_DQAA__9WtJIO) and unsafe conditions for detainees and staff, according to a Government Accountability Office report released Tuesday. The Army paid for guards, medical services, transportation, and meals at the Fort Bliss facility in El Paso for two weeks in August 2025 before [any detainees arrived](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkb2yozAMhZ_GdMrYDjGhoNiG7m67JSNsETQxmLGVv7ffcV7hNmr06Yy-Of9-ph_kyPvtL240yHtJ006vEkmE8vRKOQb_OO7s7yUti6xUPGamyWrrQDswZgrI8TO1TRhmHXrT0GC6qzHdpetNsw5z79CZ2bXLfLV2bs-OdOs6mj3OF93qhocapp0xxuiz7k8XbYNuqbsGpK6_omo1BZaUT7KS0BvLEj_pSfnk09bEYRU5ijr_UXZUdiwHecmPLSaPsbpUStlR3nWZHrLCNwMowoElKTtWStmxvqHsqL-jV3aMmG9UBNgTBBLahdMOC3qOLB94YREKsHGMnPYCuAc4HlJR5J2oAApkLneATEfKAgvvoTR5CMerHhXXqVbfNuT4VZHfFfAc7P8AAAD__570nU8), and the $1.3 billion contract required payments for 5,000 detainees even when the camp held about 1,600. The report found the camp opened without perimeter security cameras or a required inspection, and a contractor [lost a loaded firearm](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDuS5CAMhk-DM1zA-BkQbEI2m27owpZsU43BBZqm-_Zb9BUmUfLr-_T49718W-ddOP7aCzW99rgELNkjEaalxORh-7kfbnvkuO90Yt5scrgooQYuBi7lAtb599I1oFcBs2xQy3GScuzHWTanBjWNs9pgVWISvbD92kuJIGbAbtjXtXG6ysQgpZTiS8xtLxSIDscJLI7zZFknEBzF1NKJhC-bd_-OT0ztFq_G65PozuzrD1OGKVNKaR_ZUg2ZMvUapswHY8rUUUwZ8SkzU-aoonBhIF4sbSfEg2f7zhyQMJCLgW8YCBMvNhMC_7k5RS5lzy_nfc1X3GPCClgXEDO3KbknAlOmSRruUvvyMLJOHJd1_rM2_e7ZT63-BwAA___o3ZUW) that was never recovered. Three detainees have died at the facility, including one death ruled a homicide in which evidence was missing or destroyed, and a suicide that followed lapses in monitoring protocols. ICE has since replaced the original contractor, Acquisition Logistics LLC, and said the facility "is upgrading" rather than closing.
## Abbott Eyes Data Center Crackdown
Gov. Greg Abbott directed Texas utility regulators this week to shield residential electricity customers from costs tied to the state's [booming data center industry](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ_GdCDvBjAuXFxD9197JTL2Eqw4GNmbOHn7U_IKfzfSSDOfvn8_y48NMRzXv_ZOhl9bWg6qJRIz5aWmHL17nLfgbiVtG-9UnM2BFpQ4tnJsARZvQ3wvfePNKr2GhgyoCUANSkOzm5WcBL0pmPoJgMAr1N46K6cVvcaxCeYzJkcAAHmRuhsketmTmrwlpScrekk-cMod78T0smWL7_Sk3Ll0b6LZmc8iLn8EzgLnWmvn9pyOTytwXh8lHFSKwJnJ7UeK6foWONvMwUX6pHVNzK23bFtHB1NuXbbu5lM92u9fi4haD8OlO_ezycafNcQYyqhEL693G-IXhX8n8GnwfwAAAP__kCOGWQ), while also recommending broad new regulations for lawmakers to pass in 2027. In a letter to the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUC) and ERCOT, Abbott ordered that data centers [fully fund the electric infrastructure](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0b-O4yAQx_Gnwd1EA8bBFC6ucbfXXmnxZ0jQkmDBbLz79ifnFbae0Uf66vfvY_twueTn7a970MLfqW5POnohZmrbUVuJ4Wv_zOGz15T4Tj24lmlTqK6AV5Byiy6Xn00PcfEYrRxokWaW0kzGyuG-GEIZNWrjvXWjTjPFyRuLftTGU0hDXk4Mr1JKiSPay4QqoiYzR0fGzk5opJi5tgvfienb9VR-6ovaJdTHUJY7897F-EeoVaj1OI7LkZw7j0KtrnEOhYRazy6h1lKDK0Ktb0io9VZf4LyvzFBbpNZh_wpALVQGrrC3yhQY3u_QqOdIT-6QWn1AdOwg0JOpQaidT0_NBhKi9hQRRjta0OM0g7UxwhRwmqdpVGnWQ1vifuRScr8aofH2cLm8i_h3O7wW9T8AAP__V2Scjg) needed to serve their operations. The agencies must submit a joint memo on additional safeguards by July 17, and the PUC must act to reduce residential transmission costs by July 31. Abbott's legislative wish list includes requiring new facilities to add power generation to the grid, mandating water-efficient closed-loop cooling systems, requiring annual reporting on electricity and water use, and [repealing the data center sales tax exemption](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAMQL8mdBk5GRaGIsU1dHvtlchgD0QTEpR4Nuzfn9hf2MZ6kp-eLP_7nD7RBx_Xv7izk_OZpsi1BBbhPNWUAy3v4-WXV0nPp2xcFsyeJwu209BpYyZCH76ntiE3Aw2mYWf6hzH9Rz-YZnPzD3AH9wHIzETtnWjokWYwA8_QeHfFoDPGGLjDcPsAS9By_yDkfnigaoHJS8o32Vj4xPIM3-mL821JexPcJnIUdf-j7KjsWGu9vaqc11LZ8WorO8I1DCg74jwnEZ15SfvOkYoulfnwcdWEgnrhKJx15vUdUHyK2sclvOkSOPjdR5SLCwYuWvDUfPJ-XKayY5MdHdWH4EvXqxbWHX34uVN-990vZ_8HAAD__wVykRc)—projected to cost Texas $3.2 billion over the next two years. Texas has 335 existing data centers, and large projects seeking grid connections total 439 gigawatts, roughly five times the grid's all-time peak demand.
## The World Cup Is Here
The 2026 FIFA World Cup [kicks off today](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSgyAURb9GOx0eKmpBsU26bLslg7xHZEKCAySYv99hf2Hre-fcOffnqq7aefe8fesHyXzaoJ5UkqecKaoSokfzOu7O3FOwNu-UjI6OFGdcdEx0AAq18x81tig3hiu0JGFeAOZpXqHd5cQmMWyDMbQgTlrAug0bEWzDZHHhonWywpgAAGADW_uJcWQjzQtqmtdFNyMjdDnEPu-U6dTJ-k94U-xNeLRe7jkfqRm-Gn5p-KWU0ttwjlWjFhp-SUeIOdWs-nTmdXTJ7IQvT13dbqPEozjvXRJzM7LbQzv_B8__u-Qt-W8AAAD__yindl0), launching a 48-team, 104-match tournament across 16 host cities in the United States, Mexico, and Canada. The tournament runs through the July 19 final at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. Neither Texas venue hosts a game today, but the party is already on. Fair Park in Dallas opens its free FIFA Fan Festival this afternoon—big screens, food, and family viewing areas on all 34 match days through July 19. Texas hosts more matches than any other state. Harry

body:
| | | | June 11, 2026 | [Read online](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/3XJtrebpHRCGFShflIZ6RjL42i8HdHdmcZNEceKwsyr9%2FlG6u8qDwJ3b2za7%0A%2FpvOFZJQzLD%2BEsRL0n6nm8cLduFKjP%2BRQLsflTwO7D7%2BGYd6LxOtH8nlsnwj%0A%2BdBiqRngd%2Fsn%2BQOfjk8513BvmRW%2FOSmyynGqkZn8IvMav60oSotTB%2BJhdF9w%0A0LNdBlU4%2F9STcvVhu7qx0zuLqDnb19AGJw%3D%3D%0A/9e1f6a78581d30fb)

# Thursday, June 11, 2026
---
| This sponsored message from Just The Truth is on behalf of Hillsdale College [](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/wxuzfgKwJahj5j0miK%2BsPD3sE6J%2Fv71mtkO4wSTBKHRLQ3rS1xYt2wzGKy5e%0AHKLWUBRGTKZKaTds7%2BLEo%2FG2rfBfL5Gc9Gcz6AyX24%2FiL3MburIo%2FcvoWaKP%0AW3U%2Fp5BMxxY7PxRxnmiptsTn0ckkuNAm34hdDSZh7HAuSLJRsQvGNiAQSMXi%0A1DISPOREousz8HwMVvnjKHHTcPOLK3XX9w%3D%3D%0A/6dc3bd86dec6925e)Dear Friend,In the spring of 1775, a handful of farmers and tradesmen stood their ground against the greatest military power on earth.They didn’t know how the story would end.But they knew that freedom was worth fighting for.The “shot heard ’round the world” set in motion a chain of events that led to the greatest experiment in self-government the world has ever known.That’s why I’m excited to share something special with you.**The White House recently asked Hillsdale College to assist the Salute to America 250 Task Force in producing a new free video series,[_The Story of America_](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/XS%2FcIF2WsrP180P%2BrHheS2Da3NXstg1Fug0cfh92YZbsFhQ7ONY3QnuQqMGA%0Aaf6cRN7ynshhBAxvA672ARJVegJUjXFvBgHB%2FigprbEwt1cA%2BPFBcPHT%2F9Rt%0AdW%2FUzro4daAY%2B2yQahQDW904pqDsbVTASy1Rfj714rCczNmAekH0el%2BLv00k%0Aoh2IUR2OaCtqwo3B2zLglR5evuG%2FPa81kQ%3D%3D%0A/9876182d4498f40b)** —a sweeping, episode-by-episode journey through our nation’s founding in honor of its 250th anniversary.As we approach the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, this series invites you to learn about the principles, courage, sacrifice, and faith that made America possible—and _why this story still matters today_.Filmed in the historic Indian Treaty Room in the Eisenhower Executive Office Building in Washington, D.C., each episode brings a pivotal chapter of the American story to life.**Here’s a glimpse of what you can access on your journey at no cost:**
* **The Declaration of Independence** — _Larry P. Arnn, President, Hillsdale College_
How the Declaration of Independence defines who we are—and what it still asks of us
* **The Formation of the Army** — _Pete Hegseth, Secretary of War_
The moment citizen-patriots took up arms and answered liberty’s call against overwhelming odds
* **The King’s Call to Arms** — _U.S. Senator Mike Lee_
When imperial authority collided with colonial defiance—and compromise was no longer possible
* **The Culper Spy Ring** — _Brian Kilmeade, Co-Author, George Washington’s Secret Six_
The remarkable story of ordinary Americans who risked everything to outsmart the British and save the Revolution
* **Story of the American Soldier** — _Michael Knowles, Author and Podcaster_
A tribute to the forgotten men whose sacrifice secured American independence
* **The U.S. Marine Corps Birthday** — _Vice President J.D. Vance_
The enduring legacy of courage, service, and sacrifice that defines the U.S. Marine Corps

**You can receive instant access to this free video series right now using this secure link:**[**https://info.hillsdale.edu/story-of-america-free-access**](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/0YKXhxJtSADzJWThEtaEJG%2Bn5nCMrnKUzq%2FL5wUgvHDwGdzzaHfLflsr5JUq%0Ab6f20AVLhWMW4eeoASfEQ%2FqH31gswq1Gm%2BOn1Y4MlP7UvyWXWVsFn%2F5QXla1%0AXG44pk%2FUvcLX8LoiRWGyHQcqhJr%2FhBuyvP%2FJplbAfpqp4ZnvmeWLL%2BEU6Gjm%0Adjn1HXufZuQIMzzfEjVxFTfL8Lxq%2BXdd5g%3D%3D%0A/4dd2c91f3e107ce4)**As we approach our nation’s 250th anniversary, now is the time to rediscover the spirit of 1776.** And it’s my hope that, by remembering the great deeds of the past, we can inspire Americans today to equally great deeds.Enjoy your free video series!Bill Gray ’01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College**P.S.** New episodes will be released throughout the year as we approach America’s 250th anniversary—sign up now so you don’t miss a single one![**https://info.hillsdale.edu/story-of-america-free-access**](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/2yMiUGBHHEAIXbENXpLcxwtmSlreBntoZQsxaOx11cP321JhzkpYBV4HsOOm%0Azz1Ow%2B8Q3HquWyoiv2pVZnd053pYSv0RsHbGcV18JXExv7%2BmBWzQaYUw9C3s%0AbBK4%2FwCmyrW9U9gbQ66yzQKg6uBaUhw99ne%2F%2Bj4GU3YhFk9I9HK2cLwsyhr0%0A3gN%2FJP1jFd43yvxjF8ZkQZvwxY69mT12Dg%3D%3D%0A/377d469b46f061b4)

body:
Regaining the court conventionally is no longer feasible. The only path forward for Democrats is taking unprecedented action to pack the court and break the conservative stranglehold over the Supreme
| | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001yvWeDxs6-_IJQU02BA-RO02xEvKWvTY6-twjC78ZEQCfcbf96zMyWW4eFLOyF_o_6aVZaotSr8lC3WrkUxrDAir38TZ_6gn-F4nBjStYo450mckNKyoaWl4KmC3ZobDoQOfJyyRvQfnOzlLqUQFZuYjVgQyKFl6GlkUA0HEHlqrGtlhjqcMITaFD1i4xVKsTJEY86a90dn_MgPT1VEIzEweuopMTC0gNKJqsM3-3UWs=&c=CwIeAXy7tCx1CPtye_vcbSktpodlLc39IJMKOYyjqHpZAF_nq6tOXQ==&ch=HUPBjqxh7af8vcfzz4ATtnR6KFs81ClE7dq_ZMwLNSkSewlsLPwScA==)
---
|
Peter,
2065. That is how long the Conservative majority on the Supreme Court is expected to last until. Twenty-nine years from now. Children who have not yet been born will be young adults. The children you have today will be middle-aged.
Unless we do something -- the Supreme Court appears ready to issue a dark slate of rulings in favor of: a national abortion ban, an extreme crackdown on immigrants and birthright citizenship, a repeal of LGBTQ rights, and more.
By 2065, our next opportunity to regain a liberal majority, the America we know today will no longer exist:
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001yvWeDxs6-_IJQU02BA-RO02xEvKWvTY6-twjC78ZEQCfcbf96zMyWW4eFLOyF_o_6aVZaotSr8lC3WrkUxrDAir38TZ_6gn-F4nBjStYo450mckNKyoaWl4KmC3ZobDoQOfJyyRvQfnOzlLqUQFZuYjVgQyKFl6GlkUA0HEHlqrGtlhjqcMITaFD1i4xVKsTJEY86a90dn_MgPT1VEIzE42o1Zqu_825g4jEGe4oBy0=&c=CwIeAXy7tCx1CPtye_vcbSktpodlLc39IJMKOYyjqHpZAF_nq6tOXQ==&ch=HUPBjqxh7af8vcfzz4ATtnR6KFs81ClE7dq_ZMwLNSkSewlsLPwScA==)
---
And if Trump places two or three more justices before his term ends, 2065 becomes a floor, not a ceiling. That should terrify you. It terrifies us.
Regaining the court conventionally is no longer feasible. The only path forward for Democrats is taking unprecedented action to break the conservative stranglehold over the Supreme Court.
This is why Defend Our Courts exists. Our plan is the only way forward for Democrats -- and it works on two tracks simultaneously:
Track one: Win state Supreme Court races to build the firewall that protects voting rights, blocks gerrymandered maps, and holds the line at the level where elections are actually decided. We beat their machine in Pennsylvania. We beat it again in Wisconsin. We have more races to win in November and beyond.
Track two: Build the political will to unpack and reform the United States Supreme Court -- which requires winning House majorities, Senate majorities, and the presidency, because we need all three to expand the court. It's how FDR built the Supreme Court that upheld his New Deal. This is a multi-cycle fight, and it starts now.
Neither track is easy. Neither is cheap. Both are necessary. And we have already proven the model works. What we cannot do is run this program without you.
The children being born today will be adults in 2065. The America they grow up in -- whether their voice matters, whether their vote counts, whether they have more rights or fewer -- is being decided right now, in elections most people aren't paying attention to, by a court most people aren't watching.
Taking back our courts is the only way we ensure the country our children and grandchildren inherit is one that we would recognize. subject: Grant Report: June 11, 2026
body:
Trust, but Verify Your Election Vendors

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/grantdemocracy/grant-report-may-28-12773478?e=c16f400a56)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/yxYukqbd5b4?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a)
| | **Trust, but Verify Your Election Vendors****By Justin Riemer, President, USGI, and Marshal Trigg, Counsel, USGI** Maryland spent the back half of May reprinting roughly half a million primary ballots after a [coding error](https://us.list-manage.com/ALSyZD05bgz?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) by the state’s mail ballot vendor stripped party identification during ballot packet insertion. Because the vendor could not determine which voters received the wrong ballot, the State Board of Elections (“SBE”) had little choice but to reprint and remail ballots to all primary voters who had a pending mail ballot request.Although SBE was right to send replacement ballots and responded quickly, its remedial efforts appear to have outpaced the planning needed to carry them out smoothly. There have been [reports](https://us.list-manage.com/jILVbp0qrkt?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) of some [voters](https://us.list-manage.com/149lHugfNQR?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) receiving multiple replacement ballots, meaning they would have received at least three total ballots. SBE also had not entirely thought through the policy issues before remailing. For example, SBE’s position on the fate of any original ballots that voters marked and returned has evolved. It sought to ease concerns about duplicate voting by stating that all original ballots had been “voided,” leaving many to reasonably presume they wouldn’t be counted, even if the voter did not return the replacement. State Administrator of Elections Jared DeMarinis then walked back this initial position during a May 28 SBE meeting when he [stated](https://us.list-manage.com/16OiuCNhWr1?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) “at the end of the day, if all we receive back is one ballot, we will count that ballot if it’s the correct ballot.” The Board [met](https://us.list-manage.com/14nio2QElHr?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) on Tuesday to approve the modified canvassing procedures, nearly a month after discovering the problem. There are important takeaways from this mishap. First, there are inherent risks to outsourcing. It is a practical reality in modern election administration, especially in heavy vote-by-mail states that require industrial-grade ballot printing, assembly, and mailing. But outsourcing creates a natural out-of-sight, out-of-mind mindset that must be resisted. It is incumbent on states, especially those like Maryland that centralize ballot printing and mailing, to institute closer oversight and detailed standard operating procedures. State officials should also station a staff member in the facility where ballots are printed and mailed, at least for statewide elections. SBE did not but apparently sent someone to supervise the replacement ballot mailing. Maryland’s current oversight deficiencies are especially troubling given the same vendor mistakenly mailed voters [duplicate ballots](https://us.list-manage.com/Xso6uHY_Z5I?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) in the 2024 General Election. And in 2020, a previous vendor made a [proofing error](https://us.list-manage.com/oqZ2fPWMsUx?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) in a Baltimore City Council race that went undetected until the ballots were already in voters’ hands.One fix SBE should consider is a verification step the state runs itself instead of leaving it to the printer. Before the vendor mails any packets, the state could check each ballot against the voter registration file to confirm every voter is getting the correct ballot style. [North Carolina](https://us.list-manage.com/19v0axoOfhj?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a), for instance, runs every ballot style through multiple levels of county and state review before printing, with the state approving the vendor’s proofs against its own specifications rather than relying solely on the vendor. Election administrators also need to avoid the temptation to deflect blame onto vendors. SBE took on the responsibility to mail ballots for all the counties and any mistakes in fulfilling that responsibility are SBE’s alone. SBE’s [press release](https://us.list-manage.com/SxgfCXOOCdN?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) announcing the error led with blaming the vendor and SBE’s [second release](https://us.list-manage.com/AByE6oWJhWm?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) linked directly to a vendor statement. SBE, not its vendors, is accountable to the public, and its messaging should reflect that. Blaming the vendor creates the perception that SBE has distanced itself from its [statutory](https://us.list-manage.com/D0vqzL08iyR?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) responsibility to “supervise the conduct of elections” in Maryland.Finally, although SBE has gradually released more details, including the safeguards that prevent double voting, it’s too little, too late. In today’s environment, voters are highly attentive to and skeptical about our election safeguards, especially for mail voting. Merely stating that “safeguards exist” without further explanation is inherently unsatisfying and comes off as patronizing. The public demands specifics and election officials owe it to them to deliver. And dismissing those with legitimate questions about the error as misinformation spreaders is misguided.Although we are certain that SBE officials are eager to put this ill-fated primary in the rearview mirror, we hope they first look back long enough to learn from it to avoid repeating the same mistakes.
---
| | | | |
---
| | **Alabama** Following a decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit, Governor Ivey [called](https://us.list-manage.com/yQ2Ap2S7H8F?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a special primary for two state Senate districts under the state-drawn Senate map, voiding the May 19 results in those two districts.**Arizona** A special prosecutor is [investigating](https://us.list-manage.com/18cwdjR5sYt?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) whether employees of the Maricopa County Recorder’s Office illegally removed a scanner and provisional envelopes from the tabulation headquarters. The Board of Supervisors claims that the scanner belongs to its office, which the Recorder’s office disputes. **California** Counting stretched roughly a week past the June 2 statewide primary before the gubernatorial and Los Angeles mayoral races were [decided](https://us.list-manage.com/x07X9gQolyb?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a). The state’s prolonged primary vote count has [renewed scrutiny](https://us.list-manage.com/Mo1UdG3w9Fz?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) of the state’s election procedures, with election law expert Hans von Spakovsky attributing the delays to four factors: universal vote-by-mail, a seven-day deadline for receiving timely postmarked ballots, a 22-day cure period for signature issues, and the large number of provisional ballots requiring individual review. He argued these policies make extended counting periods a predictable feature of California elections. The New York Times Editorial Board also [weighed in](https://us.list-manage.com/6V_AfqQweIY?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) stating that “California has . . . adopted an approach to election administration without meaningful benefit and with substantial downside” and calling for reforms at the state and federal levels to ensure quicker vote counting processes.The controversy has also drawn [federal attention](https://us.list-manage.com/WnmSCShCjop?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a). First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli announced that the U.S. Attorney’s Office, in coordination with the FBI, has opened multiple election-fraud investigations related to California’s primary election and is auditing the state’s voter rolls. State officials maintain that the slow count reflects statutory verification and canvassing requirements rather than evidence of wrongdoing.The U.S. Postal Inspection Service [recovered](https://us.list-manage.com/1Aty3wFyrLp?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) roughly 29 voted ballots from bins of stolen mail in Santa Clara County and delivered them, still sealed in their return envelopes, to the county Registrar of Voters, which signature-verified and counted them. | | **North Carolina** Photo ID, Absentee Voting, Recount, and Voting Site RulesComment deadline: July 14, 2026 (all four sets) Absentee Voting hearing: June 22, 2026Voting Site Rules hearing: June 29, 2026The State Board of Elections has [proposed four sets of amendments](https://us.list-manage.com/9W1oFmietzM?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) under its general supervisory authority over elections (N.C.G.S. § 163-22), all open for public comment from May 15 through July 14, 2026. The Photo ID Rules (08 NCAC 17 .0101, .0109) align certain deadlines with statutory deadlines and would make a county board’s decision on an in-person or absentee photo-ID exception affidavit a majority-vote matter rather than a unanimous one. The Absentee Voting Rules (08 NCAC 18 .0201–.0505) set procedures for county staff reviewing returned absentee ballots, distinguishing curable deficiencies, non-curable deficiencies that require cancellation and reissuance, and irregularities that do or do not require contacting the voter. The Recount Rules (08 NCAC 09 .0110) change the deadline for when a county board must begin a hand-to-eye recount. The Voting Site Rules (08 NCAC 10C .0101–.0104) address buffer zones, electioneering areas, and conduct, including noise, at voting sites.

| | The U.S. Postal Service [filed](https://us.list-manage.com/YgX0OdtlPqs?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a proposed rule, “Ballot Mail for Federal Elections,” published in the Federal Register on June 2 with a 30-day comment period. The proposal would require states to submit to USPS the names and addresses of voters receiving mail-in or absentee ballots, along with unique barcodes tied to each voter’s outbound and return envelopes, and would establish a Federal Ballot Mail Portal generating state-specific participation lists. The rule would apply to general, special, and runoff federal elections, but not primaries or ballots sent to military and overseas voters, and implements the administration’s March 31 executive order.The U.S. Senate [rejected](https://us.list-manage.com/dx82eOk9fC1?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the SAVE America Act, which Republicans offered as an amendment to a $70 billion immigration-enforcement funding bill then on the floor. The measure would have required documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections, photo identification to cast a ballot, and state voter-roll checks against a federal citizenship database; it had passed the House in February. Four Republicans joined all Democrats in opposition. The Senate Democrats’ “Election Protection Task Force” [held](https://us.list-manage.com/80Z6W5Dr1QI?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) its second meeting since launching in April, a tabletop exercise with outside election-law experts rehearsing responses to scenarios the group anticipates in the 2026 midterms.

clean_body: Trust, but Verify Your Election Vendors | | | | | | | | | Trust, but Verify Your Election VendorsBy Justin Riemer, President, USGI, and Marshal Trigg, Counsel, USGI Maryland spent the back half of May reprinting roughly half a million primary ballots after a by the state’s mail ballot vendor stripped party identification during ballot packet insertion. Because the vendor could not determine which voters received the wrong ballot, the State Board of Elections (“SBE”) had little choice but to reprint and remail ballots to all primary voters who had a pending mail ballot request.Although SBE was right to send replacement ballots and responded quickly, its remedial efforts appear to have outpaced the planning needed to carry them out smoothly. There have been of some receiving multiple replacement ballots, meaning they would have received at least three total ballots. SBE also had not entirely thought through the policy issues before remailing. For example, SBE’s position on the fate of any original ballots that voters marked and returned has evolved. It sought to ease concerns about duplicate voting by stating that all original ballots had been “voided,” leaving many to reasonably presume they wouldn’t be counted, even if the voter did not return the replacement. State Administrator of Elections Jared DeMarinis then walked back this initial position during a May 28 SBE meeting when he “at the end of the day, if all we receive back is one ballot, we will count that ballot if it’s the correct ballot.” The Board on Tuesday to approve the modified canvassing procedures, nearly a month after discovering the problem. There are important takeaways from this mishap. First, there are inherent risks to outsourcing. It is a practical reality in modern election administration, especially in heavy vote-by-mail states that require industrial-grade ballot printing, assembly, and mailing. But outsourcing creates a natural out-of-sight, out-of-mind mindset that must be resisted. It is incumbent on states, especially those like Maryland that centralize ballot printing and mailing, to institute closer oversight and detailed standard operating procedures. State officials should also station a staff member in the facility where ballots are printed and mailed, at least for statewide elections. SBE did not but apparently sent someone to supervise the replacement ballot mailing. Maryland’s current oversight deficiencies are especially troubling given the same vendor mistakenly mailed voters in the 2024 General Election. And in 2020, a previous vendor made a in a Baltimore City Council race that went undetected until the ballots were already in voters’ hands.One fix SBE should consider is a verification step the state runs itself instead of leaving it to the printer. Before the vendor mails any packets, the state could check each ballot against the voter registration file to confirm every voter is getting the correct ballot style. , for instance, runs every ballot style through multiple levels of county and state review before printing, with the state approving the vendor’s proofs against its own specifications rather than relying solely on the vendor. Election administrators also need to avoid the temptation to deflect blame onto vendors. SBE took on the responsibility to mail ballots for all the counties and any mistakes in fulfilling that responsibility are SBE’s alone. SBE’s announcing the error led with blaming the vendor and SBE’s linked directly to a vendor statement. SBE, not its vendors, is accountable to the public, and its messaging should reflect that. Blaming the vendor creates the perception that SBE has distanced itself from its responsibility to “supervise the conduct of elections” in Maryland.Finally, although SBE has gradually released more details, including the safeguards that prevent double voting, it’s too little, too late. In today’s environment, voters are highly attentive to and skeptical about our election safeguards, especially for mail voting. Merely stating that “safeguards exist” without further explanation is inherently unsatisfying and comes off as patronizing. The public demands specifics and election officials owe it to them to deliver. And dismissing those with legitimate questions about the error as misinformation spreaders is misguided.Although we are certain that SBE officials are eager to put this ill-fated primary in the rearview mirror, we hope they first look back long enough to learn from it to avoid repeating the same mistakes. | | | | | | | Alabama Following a decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit, Governor Ivey a special primary for two state Senate districts under the state-drawn Senate map, voiding the May 19 results in those two districts.Arizona A special prosecutor is whether employees of the Maricopa County Recorder’s Office illegally removed a scanner and provisional envelopes from the tabulation headquarters. The Board of Supervisors claims that the scanner belongs to its office, which the Recorder’s office disputes. California Counting stretched roughly a week past the June 2 statewide primary before the gubernatorial and Los Angeles mayoral races were . The state’s prolonged primary vote count has of the state’s election procedures, with election law expert Hans von Spakovsky attributing the delays to four factors: universal vote-by-mail, a seven-day deadline for receiving timely postmarked ballots, a 22-day cure period for signature issues, and the large number of provisional ballots requiring individual review. He argued these policies make extended counting periods a predictable feature of California elections. The New York Times Editorial Board also stating that “California has . . . adopted an approach to election administration without meaningful benefit and with substantial downside” and calling for reforms at the state and federal levels to ensure quicker vote counting processes.The controversy has also drawn . First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli announced that the U.S. Attorney’s Office, in coordination with the FBI, has opened multiple election-fraud investigations related to California’s primary election and is auditing the state’s voter rolls. State officials maintain that the slow count reflects statutory verification and canvassing requirements rather than evidence of wrongdoing.The U.S. Postal Inspection Service roughly 29 voted ballots from bins of stolen mail in Santa Clara County and delivered them, still sealed in their return envelopes, to the county Registrar of Voters, which signature-verified and counted them. The agency issued a warning to voters about mail theft as counting in the June 2 primary continued.Shasta County to the Secretary of State an incident in which the county’s election official allegedly removed from the elections office copies of documents that may have contained confidential voter information; the county said the matter falls under the Secretary of State’s jurisdiction and that it will not initiate charges, and a related ballot-data discrepancy remains under review.Georgia The State Election Board a non-binding resolution encouraging counties to move to hand-marked paper ballots and approving interim guidance to that effect, a posture that conflicts with the secretary of state’s direction that counties continue using the state’s current ballot-marking devices. Board members framed the measure as a contingency should the legislature not act before a July 1 statutory deadline after which QR codes may no longer be used to count votes on Georgia ballots.Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry into law aiming to strengthen election security. On August 4, Governor Mike Kehoe is asking voters to cut taxes for the wealthy, raise them for most Missourians, and obliterate the state budget.

| |

# [Vote NO on Amendment 5](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=201207909&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjAxMjA3OTA5LCJpYXQiOjE3ODExODE3ODMsImV4cCI6MTc4Mzc3Mzc4MywiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.V--1RkMGeuRB1w0KpQ6fjZItNicELpNF7xKp1NPn4-4)
### On August 4, Governor Mike Kehoe is asking voters to cut taxes for the wealthy, raise them for most Missourians, and obliterate the state budget.
| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/@bensamuels)
---
| Jun 11
---
| [](https://substack.com/@bensamuels)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=201207909&utm_source=substack&isFreemail=true&submitLike=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjAxMjA3OTA5LCJyZWFjdGlvbiI6IuKdpCIsImlhdCI6MTc4MTE4MTc4MywiZXhwIjoxNzgzNzczNzgzLCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMjQ0MDM5OCIsInN1YiI6InJlYWN0aW9uIn0.uUwLrlY0IcyQ_-juzY0RwSDBKnwBmcS0h_g8yZn4r_4&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-reaction&r=1hvr60)

---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/bensamuels/p/vote-no-on-amendment-5-2026?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
